summary: Proxy handshake downgrade merges streaming JSON frames and drops final object on reconnect
description:
Issue summary:
Customer sees truncated last JSON object when a long SSE stream falls back to websocket during a transient proxy handshake. The stream appears complete server-side, but the client-side JSON array is missing the final object (parser error).

Impact:
- Multiple customer production requests for multi-turn document generation are returned with a missing final record (lossy).
- Affects document ingestion -> downstream indexing pipelines which rely on complete JSON arrays.
- Repro rate ~3-7% for affected sessions; customer reports spike during peak traffic and after edge deployments.

Timeline / Observed: 
- 2026-03-12 22:14 UTC: Customer reported first incident after edge deploy.
- 2026-03-13 02:07 UTC: Support reproduced with synthetic load through same corporate proxy chain.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east) -> customer behind corporate reverse proxy (CorpWAF) + CDN that rewrites headers.
- Customer using dedicated model pin (llama-2-70b-chat).

Steps to reproduce (tested by Support):
1) Start a long-running SSE session that yields an array of JSON objects (20+ objects, ~16KB total payload).
2) Force a transient connection disruption (TCP reset path / simulate proxy idle-recycle) and allow the client to reconnect.
3) On reconnect the client negotiates websocket upgrade as the path rebalances through a different edge node that prefers ws.
4) Observe client receives a partial JSON array where the final object is either concatenated improperly or missing trailing brace.

Observed behavior:
- The final object is absent or appears as a merged token sequence: e.g. "...\n},{\"id\":123\n\"content\":\"partial" instead of "...},{\"id\":123,\"content\":\"...\"}\n]".
- Client-side parser throws "Unexpected end of JSON input".
- Server-side logs indicate the stream finished successfully with send offsets up to EOF and close marker.

Expected behavior:
- On reconnect or protocol downgrade, streaming frames should preserve boundary markers and not merge trailing fragments. The client should receive a syntactically complete JSON array matching server-sent chunks.

Customer logs / sample (truncated for brevity):
- Client raw bytes around boundary (hex): 0x5D 0x0A 0x7D 0x2C 0x7B 0x22 0x69 0x64  <-- expected closing bracket 0x5D observed absent in bad cases
- Server send log: send_seq=1024..16384 EOF=1 close_reason=200:OK
- Edge proxy logs show: "downgrade: sse->ws, connection_id=Z9Y8, content-type rewritten from text/event-stream to application/octet-stream for path /v1/stream"

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Pin the session to SSE-only by forcing X-Redwood-Prefer: sse header until fix is available.
- Increase keepalive on corporate proxy to reduce mid-session rebalances.

Business impact:
- Data loss for downstream indexing, customer paused some ingestion jobs.
- Customer escalated to account team and requested timeline for a fix.

investigation_notes: Initial repro shows edge-proxy header rewrite from text/event-stream -> application/octet-stream triggers websocket fallback on reconnect.
Binary coalescing path in streaming-runtime merges last SSE fragment with subsequent WS frame when transition occurs within a small time window (<250ms).
Client parsers are strict JSON consumers expecting a closing ']' and can fail if last object missing a trailing brace or bracket.
Hypothesis: missing sentinel emission plus proxy-induced chunk coalescing leads to effective truncation of final object even though server transmit counter reached EOF.
Reproducer environment: dual-nginx chain, custom corp-proxy rules, simulated idle-recycle with tc netem 200ms flaps. Works reliably when proxy rewrites content-type.
Related regressions: search for recent commits touching streaming-runtime framing and content-type handling (reviewing changelist between 2026-03-01 -> 2026-03-10).
resolution_notes: Work-in-progress: PR introduces explicit final-sentinel emission prior to protocol downgrade and verifies runtime does not coalesce sentinel with next frame.
Short-term mitigation documented and shared (X-Redwood-Prefer: sse).

Next steps: run full cluster load test with CDN config permutations, security review for sentinel approach, and coordinate with CDN team to avoid mid-session rollouts for affected customers during business hours.
Postmortem action item: add integration test covering sse->ws fallback with header rewrites (assigned to streaming-runtime team).
